Allergies - Urban vs Rural South Africa

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
International research shows that allergies have reached epidemic levels in urban areas.

Unique Selling Point:
Research has shown that allergies have reached epidemic levels in urban areas. But a landmark SAFFA study has shown that there were diffeneces between cities and rural areas when it came to food allergies.

Summary:
At Cape Town's Red Cross War memorial Children's hospital, Professor Michale Levine head paediatric Allergology, specialising in children's' allergies and the treatment of allergies. International research has shown that allergies can be triggered by a number of things, the consumption of fast food, fried and microwaved meat and often the overuse of antibiotics and antenatal maternal smoking. Most of these people live in urban areas. Dr Levine and his team undertook a landmark study to assess why there were differences between cities and rural areas when it came to food allergies. In CT some 1000 children were screened for various alergies as part of the research. 400 children were screened in the ~Eastern Cape. Food allergy is commonly against egg, then peanuts then milk. Food allergies seem to be increasing in severity. The study confirmed that children living closer to farm animals were more protected against all kinds of allergy including food allergy.The food allergy study yielded a curve ball, some patients revealed unusual reactions to red meat. This allergy is linked to a tick bite and is know as the Alpha-Gal allergy.

Script:


11 year old Beatrice Hill from Cape Town,has suffered with food allergies from infancy… she’s learnt to live with her allergies but sometimes… things can go horribly wrong
00:01:18 We all had hot chocolate and marshmallows. Then a few hours later we were at home and my voice completely went. My dad said we should go to the hospital. It's very scary, because you kind of feel like you're going to die but you know your'e not going to die





Her allergies have also had a severe impact on the family. Her mother Dianne now keeps a strict watch over her diet…
00:00:21 It changes everything,because you have to eat. So, its sets a benchmark of anxiety where you read every single lable.


City life is fraught with challenges brought about by urbanisation and environmental ills. This has resulted in allergies reaching epidemic levels.
There definitely is a massive epidemic of allergies. We all know somebody who has a food allergy. That’s seems to be the next wave of the allergy epidemic .…
At Cape Town’s Red Cross War Memorial Children’s Hospital, Professor Michael Levin heads Paediatric Allergology - specializing in the treatment of children’s allergies.


We have had children havin near death experiences to foods every couple of months, and children sometimes have re-current episoed and we are also seeing unusual forms of food allergy.





So here’s what we already know about food allergy… international research shows that allergies can be triggered by any number of things… the consumption of fast foods… fried and microwaved meat and often the overuse of antibiotics and antenatal maternal smoking.

But here’s the catch… most of these allergies are common in people who live in cities…
With knowledge already in hand about allergies in urban areas Professor Levin and his team undertook a landmark study to assess why there were differences between cities and rural areas when it came to food allergies.
00:00:43 The reason for doing this research in urban and rural communities in South Africa is because there have been clues from other parts of the world that there’s a protective effect of, against allergies in rural communities
So in Cape Town some 1000 children were screened for various allergies as part of the research.

Then they set off for the Eastern Cape to find out why children from rural areas suffered fewer food allergies…

There, over 400 children were screened.
00:29:28
Food allergy is commonly against egg, then peanuts then milk. The food allergies seem to be increasing in severity. I now see children, instead, of them just having 1 allergic disease they now have 3 or 4 or 5 . They are having severe reactions with anaphylaxis.

But in rural areas like the Eastern Cape , the prevalence of these allergies tells an entirely different story.
00:04:43
I would put my mark on it , they are less allergic than others in urban areas.
Dr Nomthandazo Bikitsha from the children’s ward at the Zithulele hospital in Mqanduli, rural eastern cape, seldom sees children with allergies



00:04:42
Being in a rural setting, I would say does get exposure to a lot of animals, you get exposure to a lot of insect bites. Exposure to a lot of allergens would give them a bit of a robust immune system.




The study confirmed Dr Bikitsha’s assessment… Children living in rural environments were more protected against all kinds of allergy including food allergies.
00:01:31Some of the things that are possibly important include the exposure to animals that people have in rural communities.
00:01:31 There’s a massive difference in the environments between urban community and rural community and some of these factors could be protective.

But this pioneering food allergy study also yielded an unexpected curveball.

Patients revealed unusual reactions to red meat….


00:00:01 I grew up having reactions from a young age. I would have huge hives and they were so itchy
Q Did you know that it was red meat that was making you sick?

I knew because every time I ate it I would get sick.

Q Would you get sick immediately?
Yes immediately after eating.
00:01:50


Seventy year old Nowathile Boliltye has lived with this red meat allergy since the age of 15.


00:00:12 Can't you even have a tiny taste of gravy?





00:01:14 No,No, No , I cannot even have gravy or use a dish that had red meat on, I can only eat chicken.




The research team suspected the culprit to be a tick commonly found in the Eastern Cape.

Nowathile was one of the almost 90 people tested for the Alpha Gal allergy caused by tick bites

00:28:14
If you live in a rural area or you visited a n area where there are ticks and you have been exposed to a tick bite, you might have those anti-bodies and eating any form of red meat no matter how it is cooked are potentially going to cause a problem
There are certain proteins or certain factors that the tick is injecting the person that is now triggering the immune system for you to now react to red meat.
It is in this laboratory at the University of Cape Town where

Tatenda Murangi is doing the research into the Alpha Gal allergy.


So if someone is going to be having allergic reactions to red meat , we find them having anaphylactic reactions like shortness of breath stuff like that.







There are risks and benefits of living in any environment. But, with rapid urbanization, the allergy epidemic demands new treatments and specialization.
00:03:1
Whether its a rich urban environment or poor urban environment is not actually the important factor, the important factor is that it doesn’t have that close contact with the farm animals, with all the good germs that allow us to build up our immune system in a way that is protective.


But it seems that man's best friend may not be the solution either.
00:12:20
The data to exposure to pets in urban areas is very, very controversial. so dogs seem to be better at protecting you against diseases than cats are. the amount of exposure might actually be a risk factor.




Your furry friend may cause a serious allergic reaction but maintaining a clean, germ-free environment in your home, may not necessarily be the answer to remain allergy free.


00:16:04
So one of the things that we are doing wrong in urban environments , is obsessing too much about cleanliness.

*** While RESEARCH IN THE FIELD OF ALLERGIES IS growing, treatment lags behind. Immunotherapy is ONE option
00:01:57
It has only really been in the last decade or two that research into food immunotherapy has come to the fore.
***Paediatric Allergologist Dr Sarah Karahbus specializes in food immunotherapy… SHE SHOWED ME HOW THEY TREAT FOOD ALLERGIES
00:01:57


We take miniscule amounts of the food that the person is allergic to, give them a tiny little dose to begin with . A dose so small that we don’t expect it to cause any reactions. And then we build it up over weeks , over months So the goal of immunotherapy is to slowly desensitises the patient.
00:06:49
.





But perhaps a more natural approach may be the answer to preventing allergies.




00:32:01 We’ve moved to far away from nature, that we need to have exposure to soil, we need to have exposure to plants, we need to relax more, I think that we have got too far away from our roots.
